details.generic_ballot_2014: RealClearPolitics generic congressional vote, 'RCP Average' row, poll window 10/15 - 11/2: Republicans 45.6, Democrats 43.2, 'Republicans +2.4' = -2.4. No poll in the table ends after 11/2, so this is the final pre-election average. Read from the Wayback Machine capture of 2014-11-06 18:48 UTC (two days after the election; the average itself is unchanged pre-election data): https://web.archive.org/web/20141106184809id_/http://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/other/generic_congressional_vote-2170.html . The RCP page was free (not paywalled); realclearpolitics.com / realclearpolling.com itself was not fetched. Saved as raw/rcp-generic-ballot-wayback-20141106184809.html
details.generic_ballot_2014_used_and_why: RCP is used because it is the only free election-eve average found: its window closes 11/2 with every final-week poll included. The HuffPost Pollster alternative below is three days older and is the only Pollster capture between 2014-10-20 and the election.

generic_ballot_2014_alternatives.HuffPost_Pollster: 2014 National House Race, poll-tracking model estimate Democrat 44.0, Republican 45.8 = -1.8 (R+1.8), page stamp 'Updated 1 day ago' in the only pre-election Wayback capture, 2014-11-01 21:56 UTC: https://web.archive.org/web/20141101215609id_/http://elections.huffingtonpost.com/pollster/2014-national-house-race . It does not include the polls released Nov 2-3 (NBC/WSJ tie, Rasmussen R+3 through 11/2). Free page. Saved as raw/huffpost-pollster-national-house-wayback-20141101215609.html

details.congressional_2014: Clerk of the House, Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 4, 2014, 'Recapitulation of Votes Cast for United States Representatives' (50 states, November general only, Louisiana's November open primary): Republican 39,926,526, Democratic 35,368,840, total 78,812,769 = -5.783 (D 44.88%, R 50.66%). Source: https://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/2014election/ (serves the PDF), saved as raw/clerk-statistics-2014-election.pdf . The Clerk credits fusion-line votes (NY Working Families, Conservative, Independence, etc.) to those parties, not to the D/R candidate (New York 'Other Parties' 854,608).
details.congressional_2014_fec: FEC, Federal Elections 2014, '2014 Votes Cast for the U.S. House of Representatives by Party' (p. 9), general election columns. As published, 50 states (AS, DC, GU, MP, VI delegate rows removed): D 35,825,999, R 40,035,115, other 3,103,654, total 78,964,768 = -5.330; including delegates -5.103. NOT used as the headline because the table is not a clean November general: (1) per the FEC's own 'Notes on Charts' it adds the same-day unexpired-term specials in NJ-01, NC-12 and VA-07 (NJ D 92,786 R 63,727 and NC D 127,668 R 41,578 match the special-election rows exactly) and Louisiana's December 6 runoff totals; (2) Nevada's Republican and Other columns are transposed (R shown as 28,053, Other 304,809, while the FEC's own Nevada district rows give R 30,413 + 122,402 + 88,528 + 63,466 = 304,809). Swapping Nevada alone gives -5.681. Swapping Nevada, removing the three specials and replacing Louisiana with the Clerk's November figures gives D 35,368,832 and R 39,931,521, within 8 D and 4,995 R votes of the Clerk (the R gap is Indiana, FEC 793,759 vs Clerk 788,762, not traced). Like the Clerk, the FEC table does not sum fusion lines to candidates (New York D 1,788,105 in both). Saved as raw/fec-federalelections2014.pdf

No state redrew between the 2012 and 2014 elections: the sheet is labeled for both cycles, and its 2012 columns match the 2016-lines sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VfkHtzBTP5gf4jAu8tcVQgsBJ1IDvXEHjuMqYlOgYbA, saved as raw/downballot-pres2012-on-2016-lines-CHECK-ONLY.csv, not used by the derive script) in every district except Florida (27), North Carolina (13) and Virginia (5), the three states redrawn by court order for 2016.
